lines.text: I do, as I say, love these books with all my heart--and I love you too.
lines.note: Your first letter declares love for her books and for her.

lines.text: I thank you, dear Mr. Browning, from the bottom of my heart.
lines.note: Her first reply thanks you from the bottom of her heart.

lines.text: Real warm Spring, dear Miss Barrett, and the birds know it; and in Spring I shall see you, surely see you--for when did I once fail to get whatever I had set my heart upon?
lines.note: You promise that spring will bring your meeting.

lines.text: Three scratches with a pen, even with this pen,--and you have the green little Syrenusa where I have sate and heard the quails sing.
lines.note: You send her an imagined Syrenusa and singing quails.

lines.text: As to the Polkas and Cellariuses I do not covet them of course ... but what a strange world you seem to have, to me at a distance--what a strange husk of a world!
lines.note: She writes from a distance about your strange London world.

lines.text: You let 'flowers be sent you in a letter,' every one knows, and this hot day draws out our very first yellow rose.
lines.note: You send the first yellow rose in a letter.

lines.text: Pomegranates you may cut deep down the middle and see into, but not hearts,--so why should I try and speak?
lines.note: You use pomegranates and hearts as a guarded metaphor.

lines.text: It is very kind to send these flowers--too kind--why are they sent? and without one single word ... which is not too kind certainly.
lines.note: She questions your flowers sent without a single word.

lines.text: And you are NOT, NOT my 'other friend,' any more than this head of mine is my other head, seeing that I have got a violin which has a head too!
lines.note: You insist she is not merely your other friend.

lines.text: And now--here I refuse to fancy--you KNOW whether, if you never write another line, speak another intelligible word, recognize me by a look again--whether I shall love you less or more ...
lines.note: You declare love would only grow if she were lost.

lines.text: I was happy, so happy before!
lines.note: You say her gift has made you happier and richer.

lines.text: Dearest, you know how to say what makes me happiest, you who never think, you say, of making me happy!
lines.note: She says you know how to say what makes her happiest.

lines.text: Ah, the chestnut tree: do you think that I never saw the chestnut tree before?
lines.note: She recalls your earlier chestnut-tree west wind.
